extracted.intended_audience: early-career postdoctoral researchers and prospective applicants to HFSP Fellowships (Long-Term and Cross-Disciplinary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility criteria for preparing a Letter of Intent / application to HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships (Long-Term and Cross-Disciplinary), emphasizing international mobility, interdisciplinary collaborations, and frontier life-science research. Includes program priorities, eligibility constraints, funding/duration, and application portal/deadline details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel, innovative and interdisciplinary basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports novel, innovative and interdisciplinary basic research focused on the complex mechanisms of living organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should target frontier basic research in life sciences rather than applied/translational projects; novelty and interdisciplinarity are core program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on novel collaborations that bring biologists together
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear emphasis is placed on novel collaborations that bring biologists together to focus on problems at the frontier of the life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should form new collaborative groupings (not just continuing existing collaborations) among biologists and/or across disciplines to address frontier problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore new paths of research that open new areas of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to explore new paths of research that open new areas of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful projects should open up new directions of inquiry rather than incremental extensions of well-established lines; the program values intellectual novelty and boundary-pushing aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involvement of scientists from diverse (non-biological) fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasizing the involvement of scientists from diverse fields like chemistry, engineering, physics, mathematics, or nanoscience in life science projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-disciplinary input is encouraged — proposals that integrate methods, concepts or collaborators from non-biological disciplines into life-science questions are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace risk and forge research directions distinct from applicants' prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applications will embrace risk, forge innovative research directions distinct from the applicants' current endeavors...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose projects that represent a clear intellectual departure or expansion beyond their existing expertise, accepting higher risk for potential high reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internationally collaborative teams
rubrics_metrics.description: ...and involve internationally collaborative teams of researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should include international collaboration (researchers from more than one country); global teamwork is an explicit part of HFSP's evaluation of projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility requirement: work in a laboratory in a different country
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must propose to work in a laboratory that is different from the country where the doctoral degree was conferred, or first postdoctoral training was performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must plan to relocate to a host lab in a country other than their PhD country or the country of their first postdoc; mobility is mandatory and central to eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Term Fellowship eligibility (biological PhD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-Term Fellowships are for applicants with a PhD on a biological topic who want to embark on a novel and frontier project focusing on the life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants holding a biological PhD who plan to pursue novel life-science projects and meet mobility and early-career criteria should apply to this category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Disciplinary Fellowship eligibility (non-biological PhD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-Disciplinary Fellowships are for applicants who hold a doctoral degree from a non-biological discipline (e.g., physics, chemistry, mathematics, engineering, or computer science) and who would like to conduct research in the life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category targets applicants transitioning from non-biological doctoral training into life-science research; proposals should justify the cross-disciplinary move and describe how the applicant's background will contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and career stage: early-career postdoctoral researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP Fellowships span three years and are granted to early career scientists to broaden their research skills by exploring new areas of study, while working in a laboratory in a new country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be at the early postdoctoral stage (early-career) with plans to use the fellowship period to broaden skills and research horizons; the fellowship duration is three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: In both cases, the total funding amount will be about $200,000, depending on the host country. HFSP Fellowships span three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgetary expectations: plan projects and budgets consistent with ~US$200,000 over three years, recognizing country-dependent adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process and required actions (ProposalCentral account and guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested applicants must establish an account through the ProposalCentral web portal. Prospective applicants are urged to carefully review the guidelines. Deadline is 14 May 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must register on ProposalCentral, follow HFSP-specific submission guidelines, and meet the stated deadline; administrative compliance (portal account, timely LOI) is required for consideration.
